body:
### Summary

When I was making https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/22985, I noticed that the output of `uv audit --verbose` included paths prefixed by my full `${HOME}` directory (which I replaced with `~`). I think `uv` should do this itself, since we encourage people to post verbose output in bug reports. This should reduce the amount of personal information that might accidentally get posted online through verbose `uv` output.

### Example

This should be default behavior. Perhaps with a flag to disable it, just in case that's desired for some reason?

A user with the username `jdoe` who previously saw:

```text
DEBUG Found user configuration in: /home/jdoe/.config/uv/uv.toml
```

Would instead see:

```text
DEBUG Found user configuration in: ~/.config/uv/uv.toml
```

Ideally this should take atomic distributions into consideration, where the directory `${HOME}` refers to is a symlink to `/var/${HOME}`. This only affects *some* of the output. My system (which is an atomic distro) produces the user config path as in the first example above, but that same `uv` command also included a path like:

```text
DEBUG Found workspace root: /var/home/jdoe/rust-lang/fls
```

Which, ideally, would also become:

```text
DEBUG Found workspace root: ~/rust-lang/fls
```
title: Scrub home directory path from `uv` output
